A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FOG research work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support matching retained, moved, revised, and added content.

before.justification: v1 reports original pretraining experiments, loss and kurtosis trajectories, downstream benchmark scores, throughput measurements, and architecture ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds activation, mixture-of-experts, optimizer-precision, quantization, and long-context experiments.

M1.justification: The three original FOG variants remain, but Appendix D adds FOG-SwiGLU with a parameter-matched gated FFN and a sparse MoE adaptation. The latter introduces eight experts with two active, z-loss, and bias-based load balancing, substantially extending the architecture and training objective.

E1.justification: The FineWeb-Edu training corpus and nine downstream benchmarks remain unchanged. v2 adds throughput testing with 8192- and 16384-token inputs, extending the evaluated input-length scenarios beyond the original 4096-token setting.

E2.justification: The original stability and downstream comparator sets remain. v2 Table 10 adds Llama3 with blockwise FP8 scaling and includes OP with delayed FP8 scaling in the throughput comparison; OP previously appeared in stability comparisons.

E3.justification: The long run changes from 400,000 steps and approximately 419.4B tokens without cooldown to 430,000 steps and approximately 450.9B tokens with a final cooldown. Additional protocols test FP8 optimizer moments, MoE configurations, and throughput at global batch size 1024 with varying context lengths and tensor parallelism.

E4.justification: Appendices C–F substantially expand supplementary testing: a microbatch activation-range analysis examines quantization effects, FOG-SwiGLU tests dependence on activation choice, MoE experiments test architectural transfer, and FP8-moment experiments test reduced optimizer precision. The original normalization and weight-decay ablations are retained.

E5.justification: v2 adds explicit 200-step rolling-mean and 5%–95% quantile-band reporting for several training curves, including Figures 2, 4, 5, and 7. These describe temporal variability, not repeated-seed uncertainty. Existing downstream estimation errors remain unchanged, with no reported increase in independent runs.

E6.justification: Original downstream and standard-context throughput tables retain their values. v2 adds substantial results, including stable SwiGLU/MoE training, FP8-moment loss of 2.645 versus 2.649 with higher-precision moments, and batch-1024 throughput of 13.52k tokens/second/GPU for FOG-flash versus 9.48k for BF16 Llama3. Figure 7 also extends the loss trajectory under the revised training schedule.

T1.justification: New Appendix C introduces a formal tau-outlier definition, Theorem 1, and a proof claiming that larger outliers universally reduce quantization accuracy of other coordinates. v1 contains no corresponding theorem. The supplied proof does not adequately relate the scales and non-outlier coordinates of the two compared tensors.

C1.justification: The introduction adds architectural flexibility across activation families and MoE settings as an explicit contribution, broadening the original dense-model contribution scope. Claimed maximum speedup increases from 40% to 43%, and the reported long-training extent increases from 14 to 15 times the Chinchilla budget. The central fully FP8 transformer-block claim remains.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning MoE generalization and attention-related long-context efficiency. Section 6 reduces the limitations discussion to the BF16 output head, removing both the now-tested FP8-optimizer limitation and the still-relevant qualification that 8B training covers only 20B tokens.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies BF16 downstream inference and Figure 4 precision, supplies the existing xIELU formula, and documents MoE expert counts, routing coefficients, and parallelism settings. It also updates the long-run training details. The original core hyperparameter tables and repository pointer remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Apertus, GShard, and auxiliary-loss-free MoE load balancing to support the activation discussion and MoE extension. The main positioning relative to OP, SmoothSwiGLU, and prior FP8 training remains; most other reference edits supply titles or update bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: v2 places efficiency before downstream evaluation, reorganizes Section 4 under topical headings, moves the weight-decay explanation into Section 3, and adds Section 5.5 and appendix sections. Existing prose is largely retained, with localized clarification and a shortened limitations section.

P2.justification: Several existing plots are redrawn with revised colors, legends, axes, smoothing, and bands. v2 adds Figures 8–10, throughput Tables 4, 8, 10, and 11, and a boxed theorem. Retained tables and figures are also relocated and their captions expanded.

improvement.justification: The added activation, MoE, and FP8-moment tests address previously untested applicability, while the cooldown-completed long run and clearer statistical captions strengthen empirical support and transparency. These provide a limited net improvement. The gains are tempered by Appendix C's unsupported universal quantization theorem and removal of the still-valid short-training qualification at 8B.
